# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

## cand_0001 — observations that would help future runs (any capability)
- Single-iteration budget (1/1) forces bundling multiple independent fixes into one candidate, which destroys per-edit attribution: if the gate rejects, you cannot tell which of N edits regressed without the broke/fixed set being edit-granular. Suggestion: either default to ≥ a few iterations so edits can be isolated, or have the gate attribute broke/fixed to the specific diff hunk that touched each task's code path when feasible.
- Some failing tasks are unfixable from the capability edit-space: task 40 fails because the user-simulator ENDS the episode on the confirmation turn, so the agent never executes — no tool/prompt change can force an action in a turn that doesn't happen. A "task is capability-unaddressable (harness/sim artifact)" tag in the failing-task summary would stop optimizers from spending edits (and iterations) on it.
- COMMUNICATE scoring strips commas + lowercases the substring — this is critical and non-obvious for any run whose failures are communication misses; surfacing the exact matcher semantics in the capability guidance (not just discoverable by reading `evaluator_communicate.py`) would save diagnosis time.
- It would help to have a documented, ready-to-use "runner venv + tau2 src + tasks.json" path triplet in the guidance; I had to discover the venv (base python lacked pydantic/tau2) before I could verify any edit against the live DB.
